item.title: On a S-Integrable Nonlinear Evolution Equation with an Additional Algebraic Constraint
item.description: arXiv:2611.11915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a matrix nonlinear evolution equation that obeys an additional cubic constraint. That matrix partial differential equation in two independent variables is integrable in the sense of inverse scattering transform. It has a zero curvature representation with a Lax pair being a linear bundle in pole gauge and is a generalization of Heisenberg ferromagnet equation related to the special linear algebra of arbitrary rank. We prove that the scattering operator is gauge equivalent to a linear bundle Lax operator with a complex diagonal $\lambda$-leading term. We derive a few reductions e.g. a Cartan reduction, and an orthogonal reduction of the nonlinear evolution equation under consideration.
item.dc:creator: Tihomir Valchev

item.title: On transportation of constrictions on phase-lock areas of overdamped Josephson junction by means of isomonodromic deformation of the associated special double confluent Heun equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09931v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An example of computation of locations of constrictions on the phase-lock area in the parameter space for the equation modeling dynamics of overdamped Josephson junction is discussed. Several conjectures of qualitative character are inferred from the heuristic data thus obtained. The method applying isomonodromic deformations of the special double confluent Heun equation associated with the noted model is used. Such a deformation is controlled by the data provided by solution to a Third Painlev\`e equation for which a new representation in conjunction with the corresponding non-linear second order differential equation fairly efficient in the treatment of the problem in question is proposed.
item.dc:creator: S. I. Tertychniy

item.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.
item.dc:creator: Michio Jimbo, Takeo Kojima

item.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
item.description: arXiv:2611.12015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same St\"ackel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Martinusi

item.title: Global Asymptotics of a Toda Soliton Condensate with Random Scattering Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.12748v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a dense $N$-soliton condensate for the infinite Toda lattice in the limit $N \to \infty$. In contrast to previous mathematical studies of soliton gases where the norming constants are assumed to be deterministic or infinitesimal, we consider initial scattering data where both the discrete eigenvalues and the norming constants are independent random variables. The norming constants $\gamma_j$ are allowed to be arbitrarily large under a mild moment condition $\mathbb{E}[\gamma_j^\nu] < \infty$ ($\nu > 1$). Our main result is divided into two parts. First, we develop a probabilistic Riemann--Hilbert framework to show that the system self-averages: despite large, independent fluctuations in the initial data, the random Toda lattice variables converge deterministically to an effective continuum model at a polynomial rate $\mathcal{O}(N^{-\delta})$ for $0 < \delta < 1/2$. Second, by performing the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent analysis of the continuum problem, we obtain the complete leading-order macroscopic description of the lattice across the entire space-time plane. The solution decomposes into five distinct finite-gap regimes, characterized explicitly by modulated elliptic and genus-2 waves with an error of order $\mathcal{O}(1/\ln N)$. In contrast to the straight characteristic rays typical of standard soliton gas limits, the interfaces separating these five macroscopic regimes in the space-time plane are genuinely non-linear curves; in particular, the boundary of the modulated genus-2 region is completely non-linear. Finally, under our assumptions, we establish the Nonlinear Dispersion Relations for the Toda soliton condensate and prove that the macroscopic ensemble averages are determined by the soliton gas density of states.
item.dc:creator: Guido Mazzuca, Mateusz Piorkowski

item.title: $\mathrm{PGL}(3)$-invariant integrable systems from factorisation of linear differential and difference operators
item.description: arXiv:2603.18386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we present a unified approach to constructing continuous and discrete $\mathrm{PGL}(3)$-invariant integrable systems, formulated in terms of the common dependent variables $z_1,z_2$, from linear spectral problems and their factorisation. Starting from third-order spectral problems, we first provide explicit forms of the differential and difference invariants, generalising the Schwarzian derivative and cross-ratio to the rank-$3$ setting. The factorisation induces dualities among linear spectral problems, underlying the exact discretisation and multi-dimensional consistency of the associated Boussinesq systems. Then, we derive both continuous and discrete $\mathrm{PGL}(3)$-invariant Boussinesq systems, representing natural rank-$3$ generalisations of the Schwarzian KdV and cross-ratio equations. A geometric lifting-decoupling mechanism is developed to explain the reduction of these systems to the $\mathrm{PGL}(2)$-invariant Boussinesq equations. Finally, we derive a ${\mathrm{PGL}}(3)$-invariant system of generating PDEs together with its Lagrangian structure, in which the lattice parameters serve as independent variables, providing the generating PDE system for the Boussinesq hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Frank Nijhoff, Linyu Peng, Cheng Zhang, Da-jun Zhang

item.title: Discrete integrable equations with three independent variables
item.description: arXiv:2604.24100v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study nonlinear integrable equations with three independent variables of the following types: Toda-type lattices, semi-discrete lattices, and fully discrete Hirota-Miwa type models. It is shown that integrable equations of all three types admit reductions in the form of Darboux-integrable hyperbolic systems. It is important that the transition from one class to another is carried out by means of discretization (continualization) of the above-mentioned reductions with preservation of characteristic integrals. In other words, at the level of reductions, one can establish some correspondence between the classes of 3D models under consideration. In the context of this correspondence, the authors managed to conduct a comparative analysis of the well-known list of integrable Hirota-Miwa type equations, containing 13 equations. It was established that some equations from this list are related by point changes of variables. As a result, the final list of known integrable Hirota-Miwa type equations was reduced to seven. One equation was obtained by discretizing the list of semi-discrete Toda-type equations using characteristic integrals in this paper, probably it is new. For all seven models, associated linear systems (Lax pairs) are given.
item.dc:creator: Ismagil T. Habibullin, Aigul R. Khakimova

item.title: Global Analytical Solution of the Identical Kuramoto Model for N=3 via Koopman Eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2605.07360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic model of collective synchronization in coupled oscillator systems. Although its mathematical properties have been extensively investigated, explicit phase trajectories from arbitrary initial conditions have been available only for the simplest case, N = 2. In this study, we provide a global analytical solution for the phase trajectories of the all-to-all coupled Kuramoto model with three identical oscillators (N = 3). We construct Koopman eigenfunctions from products of observables whose growth rates, weighted by the exponents, sum to a constant, and obtain a nontrivial constant of motion from the ratio of two such eigenfunctions. Using their explicit exponential time dependence, we reduce trajectory reconstruction to time-dependent quartic equations and recover the phase trajectories. The same construction also yields Koopman eigenfunctions for the Kuramoto-Sakaguchi model with arbitrary phase lag and for the N = 4 all-to-all and ring-coupled systems. These results provide a concrete example in which Koopman eigenfunctions are used not only to characterize but also to explicitly solve a widely studied nonlinear model.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Taga
